lines: Most AI tools are making creators worse, not better.
I said it.
Here's why.
First, they replace human taste with average, safe output.
You start prompting instead of choosing, and the result feels like everything else.
Second, they make every video, thumbnail, and script look exactly the same.
When everyone uses the same model, nothing stands out.
I've seen it happen a dozen times.
If you use AI to think for you, you stop thinking for yourself.
That's not efficiency.
That's creative atrophy.
I know a lot of people love these tools.
They save time.
They lower the barrier.
Fine.
But speed without a point of view is just noise.
So change my mind.
Drop your take in the comments.
Let's argue.
I'll read every reply.

Even twenty pounds a month builds something real over time.

lines: Beauty isn't what the filters make it look like.
I'm sharing three things nobody tells you, and the last one is the one most people miss.
First: your skin doesn't have to be perfect to be beautiful.
It just has to be yours.
Second: expensive products don't beat consistency.
A simple routine you actually do beats a ten-step one you quit after a week.
And the best for last.
Third: beauty isn't something you chase.
It's something you notice.
It's in the way light hits your face on a Tuesday morning, not just when you're dressed up.
It's in the days you skip makeup and still recognise yourself in the mirror.
So stop trying to fix yourself, and really start looking closer.
runs.input: Three things nobody tells you about beauty

lines: I was standing in front of [my biggest client of the year], [last Tuesday morning], ready to walk them through our new pricing model.
One slide in, the screen froze.
Not a glitch. The whole demo just died.
I could see them checking their watches, already mentally packing up.
I had two choices: apologise and reschedule, or keep talking without the visuals.
I chose the second.
My heart was still racing, but I kept my voice steady.
We talked through the numbers on a whiteboard, messy and real.
By the end, they weren't just sold on the pricing.
They bought into how we handle pressure.
That day changed how I pitch.
Now I never walk into a room without a backup plan that doesn't need electricity.

_invented: I had two choices: apologise and reschedule, or keep talking without the visuals.
My heart was still racing, but I kept my voice steady.

So basically I started my fitness journey back in March 2021 when my doctor, Dr. Patel, told me my blood pressure was 150 over 95 which honestly scared me a lot. I was working as an accountant in Manchester and sitting at my desk for like ten hours a day. At first I just walked 5,000 steps every day and then I moved up to 10,000 steps and started going to the gym three times a week. My friend Jordan showed me how to deadlift properly. After about eight months I lost 14 kilos and my blood pressure went down to 120 over 80. Now I make videos for people with desk jobs because most fitness content is made for people who already love the gym. You don't need two hours a day, you need twenty minutes and consistency.
